item.title: docs.hyperlane.xyz introduction and Multisig ISM pages

findings.finding: Deployment is permissionless; ISMs are chosen per application.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "Anyone can deploy Hyperlane, whether it is a layer 1, rollup, or app-chain"; ISMs "allow developers to configure, compose, and customize their security model according to their application's needs."

findings.finding: Multisig ISM trust: m of n validators attest to a message; validator signatures are not specific to an ISM, so any ISM can use any validator running on Hyperlane.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "m of n Validators have attested to the validity of a particular interchain message"; "Validator signatures are not specific to an ISM"

item.title: docs.layerzero.network v2 security stack and DVNs

item.title: docs.chain.link CCIP billing and cross-chain token registration pages

findings.finding: Network fee for token transfers: $0.225 (LINK) / $0.25 (other) between two non-Ethereum chains, $0.45/$0.50 from Ethereum to a non-Ethereum non-Solana chain, $1.35/$1.50 from a non-Ethereum chain to Ethereum, $0.315/$0.35 to Solana from non-Ethereum; messaging non-Ethereum to non-Ethereum $0.09/$0.10; token pool owners may add flat USD or bps fees.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Token transfers or programmable token transfers | Not Ethereum | Not Ethereum or Solana | $0.225 | $0.25

findings.finding: Token registration is self-service with no Chainlink step if the token exposes owner(), getCCIPAdmin() or DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: the caller proposes itself via RegistryModuleOwnerCustom, accepts the admin role in TokenAdminRegistry, deploys its own pools and calls setPool.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "The CCT standard is self-service for tokens that support one of the recognized administrator registration patterns."; "Token developers deploy, configure, and manage their own token pools without intervention from CCIP."

findings.finding: Relayers front their own capital on the destination chain; a Dataworker bundles fills and proposes them to the HubPool on Ethereum with a bond; UMA's Optimistic Oracle accepts unless disputed within a window; relayers are repaid about every 1.5 hours; fixed fees, so relayers compete on speed.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "Only a single honest actor needs to dispute an invalid proposal."

notFound: challenge window length and bond size

findings.finding: Status Draft, created 2024-04-11; current text centres on IResolver.resolve(bytes payload) returning a ResolvedOrder; earlier IOriginSettler and IDestinationSettler types were removed; it standardises order description, not settlement.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "function resolve(bytes calldata payload) external view returns (ResolvedOrder memory);"; "does not require protocols to use a common escrow, settlement contract, or fill function."; "does not standardize or guarantee the security of the protocol that ultimately settles the order."

findings.finding: Interop is described as in active development and rolled out iteratively; messages are an initiating log on the source chain and an executing message through the CrossL2Inbox predeploy on the destination; each chain declares a dependency set; no mainnet date is given on the page.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "OP Stack interop is in active development. Some features may be experimental."; "The Superchain interop cluster is being rolled out iteratively."

findings.finding: The RMN contract (proxy plus implementation) keeps a registry of cursed subjects, normally chain selectors; a curse is "A manual onchain safety flag set via the RMN contract" after which sends and executions involving the lane revert; Router, OnRamp, OffRamp, token pools and verifiers check it. The page states that 16 node operators belong to the Committee Verifier; token pools enforce per-chain rate limits with separate buckets for faster-than-finality transfers.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "sends and executions involving it revert until the curse is lifted."

notFound: RMN node count and quorum (page does not give a figure)

findings.finding: Hashi aggregates hash oracles from several bridges: adapters wrap each mechanism, ShoyuBashi lets an owner set a threshold of adapters that must agree on a hash for a domain, Yaho dispatches messages and Yaru lets anyone execute them; audited by G0, Omega and Least Authority.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "Define a threshold of adapters that must agree on a hash for each domain."

findings.finding: Axelar is a proof-of-stake network whose validators vote on confirmations and, holding key shares in proportion to stake, authorise gateway execution when a threshold is reached.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "the amount of shares is dictated by the amount of staked AXL tokens the validator has."

notFound: Interchain Token Service permissionless deployment (page silent)

findings.finding: deBridge describes a non-custodial execution layer with a 0-TVL design where solvers supply liquidity per order in the deBridge Liquidity Network; users can cancel an unfulfilled order; 25+ chains and over 20 billion USD volume claimed; Solana appears as an example chain; Gnosis and Hive are not mentioned.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "0-TVL architecture where competitive solvers provide liquidity on-demand, with no shared liquidity pools."

item.title: cosmos/ibc repository README and docs/1-introduction, docs/2-how-ibc-works (raw.githubusercontent.com)

findings.finding: IBC lets two chains each verify the other's writes with an on-chain light client; relayers are off-chain transport; verification can range from consensus light clients to permissioned attestation; implementations exist for Cosmos, EVM chains and Solana; claims 115+ networks and 50 billion USD volume over five years without an exploit of the supported version.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "each chain verifies the other chain's writes with an on-chain light client."; "Flexible verification mechanisms, ranging from trust-minimized light clients to permissioned attestation-based models"

findings.finding: Open-source Solidity contracts plus a reference solver and UI implementing ERC-7683 across EVM chains with pluggable settlement layers.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "A modular, open-source framework for permissionless, scalable intent execution."

findings.finding: UniswapX is a same-chain swap settlement protocol with signed orders and competing fillers through order reactors; the README read does not describe cross-chain settlement.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: "UniswapX is an ERC20 swap settlement protocol that provides swappers with a gasless experience, MEV protection, and access to arbitrary liquidity sources."
